# frontier-wire

> An openly automated, bilingual (RU + EN) news wire covering AI, tech, science, world, culture and economy.
> Written twice a day by a scheduled agent from real, cited sources. Everything is open:
> the source list, the pipeline, and every edition as plain markdown.

Publisher: Danila Katalshov — https://adanman.github.io

## Machine-friendly entry points
- RSS feed: https://adanman.github.io/frontier-wire/feed.xml
- JSON Feed (with raw-markdown pointers): https://adanman.github.io/frontier-wire/feed.json
- Latest edition, plain markdown index: https://adanman.github.io/frontier-wire/latest.md
- Sitemap: https://adanman.github.io/frontier-wire/sitemap.xml
- Raw markdown of every article: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ADanMan/frontier-wire/main/editions/<YYYY>/<MM-DD>/<NN-slug>.md
- Source list (RSS feeds we read): https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ADanMan/frontier-wire/main/feeds.txt
- Edition format spec: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ADanMan/frontier-wire/main/FORMAT.md
- Repository: https://github.com/ADanMan/frontier-wire

## Latest articles
- [Google Search gains Gemini 4 Hydrogen](https://adanman.github.io/frontier-wire/e/2026-11-13/01-hydrogen-search.html) — The announcement targets complex questions, while individual answers still need verification.
- [ISS crew prepares Dragon to return research samples](https://adanman.github.io/frontier-wire/e/2026-11-13/02-dragon-return-preparations.html) — NASA describes cargo packing and suit maintenance, with spacecraft departure still ahead.
- [Navajo Reservoir rises sharply after autumn rains](https://adanman.github.io/frontier-wire/e/2026-11-13/03-navajo-reservoir-rise.html) — Satellite views show water gains, while short-term drought relief does not erase every long-term deficit.
- [llama.cpp 1.0.0 makes library compatibility boundaries clearer](https://adanman.github.io/frontier-wire/e/2026-11-13/04-llama-library-versioning.html) — The team establishes explicit version rules for public interfaces, while application upgrades still need validation.
- [LLMON marks instructions and data as different context components](https://adanman.github.io/frontier-wire/e/2026-11-13/05-llmon-structured-context.html) — IBM introduced experimental Granite previews, with learned separation distinct from enforced security guarantees.
- [Mangroves rebound globally while regional losses persist](https://adanman.github.io/frontier-wire/e/2026-11-13/06-mangrove-rebound.html) — NASA examines a long satellite record, without implying that the reported expansion happened today.
- [Gemini Decisions API scores options instead of writing an answer](https://adanman.github.io/frontier-wire/e/2026-11-12/01-gemini-bounded-decisions.html) — Google introduced bounded choices with probabilities, whose usefulness needs validation on the intended task.
- [Training search models for the compressed representation they will use](https://adanman.github.io/frontier-wire/e/2026-11-12/02-pooling-aware-search.html) — A Sentence Transformers example compares quality at a matched vector budget without settling results for another corpus.
- [A Hubble lens gallery frames questions for Roman observations](https://adanman.github.io/frontier-wire/e/2026-11-12/03-hubble-roman-lens-gallery.html) — NASA shows varied gravitational lenses, with dark-matter tests remaining a research objective.
- [Flow Country shows why an unassuming landscape stores so much carbon](https://adanman.github.io/frontier-wire/e/2026-11-12/04-flow-country-peat-carbon.html) — NASA published a 2024 Landsat view explaining the role of waterlogged peatlands.
- [NASA photographers revisit Endeavour’s final ferry flight](https://adanman.github.io/frontier-wire/e/2026-11-12/05-endeavour-photographic-history.html) — The November 12 account connects the 2012 photography with a forthcoming museum display opening.
- [NASA announces lunar contracts and development of PROMISE](https://adanman.github.io/frontier-wire/e/2026-11-08/01-moon-base-contracts.html) — The package combines contract frameworks, task orders and future demonstrations at distinct programme stages.
- [NASA opens applications for a new astronaut candidate class](https://adanman.github.io/frontier-wire/e/2026-11-08/02-nasa-astronaut-applications.html) — Applications close December 3, with final selection expected in late 2027.
- [GitHub makes its Slack and Teams coding integration generally available](https://adanman.github.io/frontier-wire/e/2026-11-08/03-github-chat-integration.html) — The November 6 release includes Canvas and conversation improvements, while a created PR still needs review.
- [ASUS announces a compact external Radeon with 16GB of memory](https://adanman.github.io/frontier-wire/e/2026-11-08/04-asus-usb4-graphics.html) — XG Core connects through USB4, with host and application compatibility requiring separate checks.
- [IBM brings Quantum System Two online at a Chicago laboratory](https://adanman.github.io/frontier-wire/e/2026-11-08/05-ibm-chicago-quantum-system.html) — The system is operating at Hyde Park Labs, while relocation to IQMP remains a future step.
- [NASA opens a $1 million lunar student design challenge](https://adanman.github.io/frontier-wire/e/2026-11-08/06-moon-base-student-challenge.html) — Registration runs to January 25, while a concept competition remains distinct from ordering flight hardware.
- [AST SpaceMobile plans its own Blacklift launcher](https://adanman.github.io/frontier-wire/e/2026-11-08/07-blacklift-development-plan.html) — The November 6 primary release describes future development using Firefly engines, with launch still ahead.
- [Today’s APOD revisits a European fireball from 2017](https://adanman.github.io/frontier-wire/e/2026-11-08/08-apod-fireball-observation.html) — The image appears on November 8, 2026, without reporting a new fall.
- [BioBasicsBench tests when laboratory evidence cannot support an answer](https://adanman.github.io/frontier-wire/e/2026-11-07/01-biobasicsbench-lab-evidence.html) — OpenAI introduced 100 tasks, while analysis scores remain distinct from readiness for independent laboratory work.
